walkthroughs.body_html:
Philosophy of Religion: The Nature & Influence of Religious Experience — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Philosophy of Religion: The Nature & Influence of Religious Experience brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Philosophy of Religion: The Nature & Influence of Religious Experience.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What are James's four characteristics of mystical experience?
options: Religious experiences are just hallucinations caused by stress.
Religious experiences only happen during dreams.
Ineffability (beyond words), noetic quality (gives knowledge), transience (temporary), and passivity (feeling acted upon by something greater).

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.
If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
